hero.title: Tuvis

hero.lamps: Red = awaiting approval · Amber = running · Green = done
compare.title: Without Tuvis vs with Tuvis
compare.w1d: Five windows, manual refreshing — you are the monitor.
compare.w2d: Approval requests sit unseen in the terminal and the whole night stalls; once you're out, the desktop agents are beyond reach.
compare.w3d: Some tools have no mobile app at all; the ones that do only pair with their own desktop — relearn everything with each switch.
compare.w4d: The same Skill copied eight ways, edits missed in seven, versions drifting apart.
compare.w5d: Which model burned the budget? You find out when the month ends.
compare.t1d: Eight tools' status lights on one screen — scan the whole field at a glance.
compare.t2d: Tap Allow on your phone and the agent keeps running — status synced, work never stalls.

features.title: Four gauges on the deck
features.board.desc: A red/green board for 8 AI coding tools: running, awaiting approval, done. Cards jump to the terminal or app.
features.remote.desc: Check states, send messages, queue, approve remotely, switch permission modes from your phone.
features.res.desc: One repository mapped onto every tool; preset groups switch per task.
features.pet.desc: Beibei and Starry Dew watch states and nudge approvals; the ledger tracks spend by tool, project and supplier.
oss.title: Open source · Local first · No telemetry

demo.title: Interactive demo
demo.desc: Press Play to watch the script, or click around — it's all an interactive simulation.
demo.takeover: Taken over: script paused, click freely
demo.detail.d1s1: The board is the overview: one light per card — red = awaiting approval (breathing), yellow = running, green = done; the summary row totals sessions and waits live.
demo.detail.d1s2: Waiting triggers a system-level desktop notification, so Claude's approval request never sits unseen in a terminal.
demo.detail.d1s3: Claude Code opens in full session form: three-line header, highlighted user message, collapsible thinking, the reply, the auto-mode input line — plus a desktop toast bottom-right.
demo.detail.d1s4: The Codex app window: a ChatGPT Work sidebar with task trees for tuvis-website / deepseek-harness, and the content area resting on the "What does this project do again?" plan card.
demo.detail.d1s5: The full Kimi Code TUI: a seven-line welcome box (Version / MCP connected), the Kimi Code Desktop promo with /desktop, two green MCP lines, thinking and a path-highlighted reply, and a GLM-5.3-Flash status bar with context headroom at the bottom.
demo.detail.d1s6: The WorkBuddy app window: task & space lists, the Buddy station card, and the "What model are you" chat with the action row and Hy4 preview input — the real app's look.
demo.detail.d1s7: The ZCode task window: projects grouped on the left (tuvis-app / tuvis-docs / tuvis-website), the event stream on the right — thinking, terminal commands, todos, subagents, down to done.
demo.detail.d2s1: The remote board page: header linked to MateBook16s, status pills sort the field at a glance — red awaiting, amber running, green idle.
demo.detail.d2s2: Tap a card for the detail page: the summary bar collapses process messages, thinking folds separately, the chat stays complete.
demo.detail.d2s3: The red approval card shows the exact command; tap Allow — the terminal's option list collapses, ✓ Approved prints, work resumes. Computer untouched.
demo.detail.d2s4: Messages queue instantly: the bubble lands marked "queued", the terminal shows your input line, and it runs the moment the terminal is free.
demo.detail.d2s5: Plan mode in one tap: the banner lights up and the terminal switches to the "Ready to code?" options — read-only planning, no file changes.
demo.detail.d2s6: Question cards don't interrupt: the terminal holds numbered options with descriptions (Enter to select); pick and submit from the phone.
demo.detail.d2s7: The file preview panel: file tree on the left, colored diff on the right — review changes even from your phone.
demo.detail.d3s1: Skills, MCPs and plugins all live in the Tuvis repo — edit once, effective everywhere; presets switch a tool's dispatch combo in one click; ~/.agents and Manifest installs are both entries.
demo.detail.d3s2: Import from tool dirs: a scan of ~/.claude/.codex/.kimi and friends gathers stray Skills / MCPs into the one repo — the health card flashes green and the counts climb.
demo.detail.d3s3: Manual toggle: clicking any cell enables/disables that resource for that one tool only — no other tool's column moves.
demo.detail.d4s1: Import a pet: the petdex store with three tabs (Favorites / petdex / Installed) and a real petdex.dev link — pick a buddy and import it locally.
demo.detail.d4s2: Switch pets: the grid dialog mirrors the real "switch pet" settings UI — built-in Foxbell v2 plus simulated entries; tap to swap.
demo.detail.d4s3: An approval arrives: the resident head card flips from a yellow "running" dot to a pulsing red "waiting", the pet switches to its waiting pose, and a desktop notification pops in sync.
